readmeExcerpt:
# G2Ray

> Only works in places where you can open GitHub Codespaces

## ⚠️ Important Notice

**Please read this before using this project:**

This project creates and runs a V2Ray proxy server. While the intention is for legitimate use, **we strongly recommend using a separate GitHub account (not your main account) when forking and running this project**, as GitHub may restrict accounts that violate its terms of service.

## Overview

G2Ray is an automated setup for running a VLESS proxy through GitHub Codespaces. It provides a quick way to set up your own proxy server for accessing content from restricted regions.

## Setup

1. **Create or use a secondary GitHub account** (highly recommended)
2. Fork the repository to your account
3. Click the green **"Code"** button above
4. Go to the **"Codespaces"** tab
5. Click **"Create codespace on main"**
6. Wait for the setup to complete (usually 2-5 minutes)

## How to Use

1. **Wait for Codespace initialization** - The setup process takes a few minutes. All dependencies and configurations will be installed automatically.

2. **Get your VLESS link** - Once ready, your VLESS proxy link will be printed directly in the terminal

   

3. **Import the link** - Copy the generated VLESS link and import it into:
   - V2RayNG (Android)
   - Clash Meta
   - Or any other proxy application that supports VLESS

## Important Notes

### GitHub Codespaces Quota
- GitHub provides **120 free compute hours per month** (per core)
- For a 2-core Codespace: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 hours/month
- **Stop your Codespace when not in use** to preserve your hours
- You can always restart it later when needed

### Compatible Networks
Tested on Shecan (free plan). If these IPs work for you, the proxy should be functional:
- `63.141.252.203`
- `50.7.5.83`
- `94.130.50.12`

If these IPs don't work, try different datacenters or ISPs from your region.

### Troubleshooting
- If the Codespace fails to start, try creating a new one
- Check that your GitHub account has Codespaces enabled
- Ensure you have enough compute hours remaining for the month
- For network issues, try switching proxy protocols in your client app

## Support the Project

If you find this project useful, consider supporting its development:

## Disclaimer

This tool is provided for educational and legitimate use only. Users are responsible for complying with their local laws and regulations regarding proxy usage. The author is not responsible for any misuse or legal consequences arising from the use of this tool.

## License

This project is open-source. Please check the LICENSE file for details.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An automated setup tool for deploying a temporary, cloud-based VLESS proxy server using GitHub Codespaces.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: G2Ray streamlines the complex process of deploying a personal V2Ray (VLESS) proxy server by cleverly leveraging the free compute resources provided by GitHub Codespaces. Upon launching a Codespace from a forked repository, the tool executes an automated setup script that installs and configures all necessary networking dependencies within a few minutes. It then directly outputs a ready-to-use VLESS proxy link into the terminal, bypassing the need for personal infrastructure, credit cards, or complex manual server administration. This approach provides a rapid, cloud-based solution for circumventing network censorship effectively.
keyFeatures: Automated Codespace Deployment: Executes all installation and server configuration processes automatically the moment the Codespace environment starts.
VLESS Protocol Generation: Creates a secure, standard VLESS proxy link that integrates effortlessly with popular clients like V2RayNG and Clash Meta.
Zero-Infrastructure Dependency: Operates entirely within GitHub's free monthly compute quota without requiring any VPS rental or payment information.
Terminal Output Integration: Displays the generated, configured proxy link directly in the integrated web terminal for immediate, simple user access.
Rapid Server Initialization: Completes the full server configuration, dependency installation, and startup process in approximately two to five minutes.

useCases.title: Temporary Secure Browsing
useCases.description: Travelers quickly spin up a cloud-based proxy on untrusted public Wi-Fi networks to secure their traffic without purchasing a commercial VPN.

useCases.title: Proxy Client Testing
useCases.description: Network developers generate a temporary VLESS backend instantly to test the connection and import capabilities of custom routing applications.

useCases.title: Educational Exploration
useCases.description: Students safely analyze the automated deployment scripts to learn about remote server configuration and the inner workings of the VLESS protocol.
